vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: akshare-api
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is classified as suspicious due to the presence of a portfolio management feature in `main.py` that uses `subprocess.run` to execute a script located in a parent directory (`../a-stock-analysis/scripts/portfolio.py`), which is a risky lateral execution pattern. There is a notable discrepancy between the `SKILL.md` instructions, which explicitly advise the agent not to use the skill for portfolio management, and the `main.py` code which implements the logic to do so. Additionally, all user queries are transmitted to a hardcoded external service at `https://akshare.devtool.uk`, which, while consistent with the stated purpose, centralizes user data on an external endpoint.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (query market data) but routes all queries to an opaque third‑party endpoint and includes a local 'portfolio' branch that runs external scripts — both of which are disproportionate and warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (market data and analysis) matches the code's primary behavior: classify a query and POST it to a remote Akshare-like service. However, the code also includes a local 'portfolio' management branch that executes a script outside the skill (../a-stock-analysis/scripts/portfolio.py). The SKILL.md explicitly says portfolio management is not suitable to expose, yet the code still implements it — an inconsistency that deserves attention.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run python3 main.py --query "..." and to always use the fixed service URL https://akshare.devtool.uk. That means every user query (including any sensitive or identifying text) will be POSTed to that third‑party endpoint. The instructions also forbid changing the service URL, removing the user's ability to point the client to a trusted/self‑hosted service. The code additionally contains logic to run a local portfolio script (subprocess), potentially accessing local state if that script exists.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only + included Python files). No packages are downloaded during install. Risk comes from runtime behavior (network calls and potential subprocess execution), not from an installer that fetches arbitrary code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials, but it nevertheless exfiltrates queries to an external host (https://akshare.devtool.uk) by default. For market data this might be reasonable, but the domain is not the well‑known akshare project domain and the skill forbids changing it — this is disproportionate transparency for a data‑lookup skill. Also, the portfolio branch runs an external local script (outside the skill), which could access local files/credentials if present.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and uses the platform default for autonomous invocation. It does not modify other skills or system configs. However, it can execute a local script via subprocess when 'portfolio' intent is detected, which gives it the ability (when that external script exists) to run arbitrary local code — a risk that depends on the environment where the agent runs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing or invoking this skill consider the following:
- All user queries are sent to https://akshare.devtool.uk. That domain is not the official akshare GitHub/pypi project; treat it as an opaque third‑party service. Do not send sensitive or private holdings/IDs unless you trust that service.
- The SKILL.md intentionally forbids changing the service URL, but the code hardcodes and uses that URL anyway. If you need to self‑host/inspect the backend, get the author to provide a configuration option or source for the service implementation.
- The skill includes a 'portfolio' branch that calls a script at ../a-stock-analysis/scripts/portfolio.py. If that script exists on the host, it will be executed. Audit or remove that path if you do not want the skill to be able to run local scripts.
- If you require stronger assurance: (1) review/modify the code to point to a known/trusted service (or allow service-url override), (2) remove or sandbox the portfolio subprocess calls, and (3) run the skill in an environment with restricted network and filesystem access until you are comfortable with its behavior.
- If you are unsure who published this skill (source is unknown), treat network egress of your queries as the main risk and prefer alternatives that call official, verifiable APIs or that allow self‑hosting.
